newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat futures ease on U.S. decline, rain.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat futures ease on U.S. decline, rain.

text.p: Australian wheat futures quotes tended lower on Monday on a combination of a decline in Chicago on Friday and weekend rain that partly eased some drought fears.
"The market was in line with the fall in in the U.S. on Friday," Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd said.
In addition, rain in Victoria and southern New South Wales on the weekend eased a few concerns about the prospects of drought in the coming planting season, he said.
Trade was quiet though, with only one lot traded, in January 1998 futures at A$185.50 a tonne, down A$1.50. Most settlement prices declined by a range of A$1.50 to A$3.50.
